question.problem:
Consider the function $y=(\operatorname{tan}⁡x)^{x}.$ Its derivative is given by  

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}=(\operatorname{tan}⁡x)^{x}\cdot g(x).
$$

Find the function $g(x).$

current_example.problem: Find the derivative of the function $y = (x^2-1)^x.$
current_example.worked_solution:
We have the function 

$$
y = (x^2-1)^x.
$$

First, we take the natural logarithm of both sides:

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{ln}⁡y & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(({x}^{2}-1)^{x}) \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡y & =x\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2}-1)\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we differentiate both sides with respect to $x{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{ln}⁡y) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(x\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2}-1)) \\ \frac{1}{y}\cdot \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(x)\cdot \operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2}-1)+x\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2}-1)) \\ \frac{1}{y}\cdot \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =1\cdot \operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2}-1)+x\cdot (\frac{1}{{x}^{2}-1}\cdot 2x) \\ \frac{1}{y}\cdot \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2}-1)+\frac{2{x}^{2}}{{x}^{2}-1}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we solve for $\dfrac {\textrm{d}y}{\textrm{d}x}{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =y(\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2}-1)+\frac{2{x}^{2}}{{x}^{2}-1})\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we substitute $y = (x^2-1)^x{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =({x}^{2}-1)^{x}(\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2}-1)+\frac{2{x}^{2}}{{x}^{2}-1}) \\  & =({x}^{2}-1)^{x}(\frac{({x}^{2}-1)\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2}-1)}{{x}^{2}-1}+\frac{2{x}^{2}}{{x}^{2}-1}) \\  & =({x}^{2}-1)^{x-1}(({x}^{2}-1)\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2}-1)+2{x}^{2})\end{aligned}
$$
